question: Scanning 30 items at 40 ms each and stopping at a randomly placed target, how many ms longer is 'absent' than an average 'present'?
move: Proving something is absent takes far longer than finding it.
trap: 600, taking an average 'present' to need exactly 15 checks.
hint: Ask at which position, on average, a randomly placed target turns up.
steps: 'Present': the target is equally likely at positions 1 to 30, so on average (1 + 30) / 2 = 15.5 checks.

diagram.caption: Saying 'absent' means checking all 30 items: 580 ms longer than an average find.

reference: Treisman & Gelade, A feature-integration theory of attention, Cognitive Psychology, 1980
